tldr: This is a loose topical cluster, not one event: four independent items that each use "routing" to cut inference cost, latency or capacity risk at a different layer. OpenRouter rebuilt provider routing on Oct 30, a Show HN introduced the Sibyl local appliance on Nov 7, and the C²-Routing paper applied routing to VLM inputs on Nov 10.
whats_new: AWS describes how Salesforce uses the SageMaker AI cross-Region inference router (Nov 18) to pool fragmented Regional capacity, adding capacity across Regions and accounts for reliable model serving.
why_it_matters: "Routing" now names four separate levers (which provider serves a request, which local backend runs it, how much input reaches the model, and which Region has capacity), and each is tuned, evaluated and failed over differently.

beats.headline: OpenRouter rebuilds provider routing for better, faster inference
beats.summary: Routing at the hosted-gateway layer: choosing which provider serves a request.

beats.headline: Sibyl packages a local inference stack as an immutable appliance with routing
beats.summary: A solo side project, described by its author as early days, that puts routing in a portable self-hosted box configured through a UI.

beats.headline: C²-Routing applies routing to VLM inputs: cropping plus compression
beats.summary: A paper on model-agnostic input reduction for visual question answering, unrelated to the products around it.

beats.headline: Salesforce routes SageMaker AI inference across Regions and accounts
beats.summary: A vendor case study on routing for capacity: spreading model serving across AWS Regions when one Region runs short.

open_questions: Does OpenRouter publish latency or success-rate numbers that quantify the rebuilt provider routing?
Does Sibyl's routing select among local models and backends only, or can it also fall back to hosted providers?
How much accuracy does C²-Routing give up for its input reduction, and does the result hold across VLMs beyond those the paper tests?
What added latency and data-residency constraints come with SageMaker AI cross-Region routing, and does AWS publish failover numbers beyond the Salesforce account?
take_for_builders: Treat these as four independent decisions. If you serve on SageMaker AI and hit Regional capacity limits, check cross-Region routing against your data-residency rules and measure the added latency; re-measure OpenRouter traffic after its routing rebuild.
